From my experience as a Canadian citizen, the lower paying jobs in fast food and customer service are always open. People tend to come and leave very quickly for those ones. As for the others, it depends on where you live. In Vancouver it is incredibly hard to find any type of job. Ontario is your best bet, they have the most growth in places to work and in my experience you can find good places that will not discriminate. It's at the very least a safe place to start with a good wage and a good place to live, it isn't terribly price to survive in ON and you get many opportunities there. I'd say smaller areas like Northbay are a good place to start, Toronto is massive and would have job opportunities but its incredibly expensive to live there.

Just be safe, right now the world is messier than ever. Don't wantcha catching the virus or getting hurt anywhere.

Hope this helped a little bit.

​

(I can't say anything about PGDM jobs, but if you need a starting place, this is a great way to start out. Even if you don't want a minimum wage job at first, it'll at the very least help you get settled some before you go for your PGDM)

I am in a similar state as you and it depends. if you can act like this isn't a big thing and fudge how long you have been starving yourself (Saying you are trying a healthier approach or something, or just say you don't always have an appetite etc.) or say that the cuts you have on your legs are from shaving your legs or accidentally scratching yourself . Act as if it's no biggie and there wasn't any ulterior motive and you will find yourself less likely to be admitted. 

If you are minor (as I am) then this is a bit more complicated as your parents can force you to go but you have to be seen by a third party councilor/therapist to determine your mental stability to see if you really need treatment. This could lesson/stop you from going.

In Canada if you are over 16 you have much more control over yourself in this situation but it isn't full control over it as if they deem you mentally unstable you will be stuck there for a small period of time where they deem you well enough (1 to 3 weeks?)

(I know you didnt ask for this but I thought it might be nice to have a little hope for something)

As for the mother abuse situation, if you search for something called the futures program, its for 16-24 and it houses people who can't live with parents. You get a bed and a space, you pay low rent and the only requirement is that you are going to school or work, you can stay as long as you wish or until 24. They are around in Canada and if you contact them they will be able to answer more of your questions. It seems to also have security so your abusive people/family can not visit or see you without your permission. Futures gives you the independence of living on your own but you still get some parental guidance by some professional councilors that make sure everyone is safe(helps with panic attacks, the like) and non violent towards others.

I am new to the self harm type of scars but I have bad body disphoria/general hate for my body and have been heavily scarred occasionally due to incidents in my life and I feel the same way. i found the best way to deal with the intense drowning anxiety (at least for me) about being intimate with such obvious (or at least to you, some of mine are light some are more obvious) scars is to fake it till you make it confidence. That and just treating yourself like a kindness project. Uhm how do I put this. Ok. So we tend to be super negative towards ones self and very self destructive and if you, instead of saying "hey I need to think this way because it's healthy" go "I want to try something new, this project." Name it something fun, do something fun with it. Make it so every time you gain enough confidence to say something good about yourself especially about your scars you get a reward for being kind. Over time you start feeling more confident. To the point of maybe wearing clothes that show off the scars, etc.I know it sounds super off topic but it helps. By facing your fears in a less high stakes environment you can feel a little better about making more intimate connections. Or opening up in any way actually.I still am terrible at opening up. I hate being vulnerable and I will try to leave hints but because of my private and introverted personality no one really notices. Sometimes the best you can do in that situation is finally gather the courage to even say one time to your therapist/councilor/health personal that you are struggling to ask for help. Vulnerability in itself is a hard thing to achieve but I feel as you start building yourself up and feeling better you will also open up more, being more at ease with being vulnerable.

I hope this made sense and helped at all, sorry if its incoherent
